# The map

Which MRI physics this scanner covers, and which task asks for which piece of it.

The list holds 110 pieces of MRI physics and applied MR physics, as textbooks and curricula name them. The scanner forms 61 of them and 11 more in part. The other 38 are not formed yet: 7 of them the package already computes and checks without serving them, and [the last list](#not-formed-yet) says which piece of engine work each one waits for. No image of this engine has been compared with a measurement on a scanner yet.

## On one screen

Rows: what you need to know. Columns: what you do with it. A cell holds the tasks; *italic* means in construction, not playable yet.

Listed: items on the map. Formed: an agent meets it at the console, and a check that exists shows it. Isolated by a task: one task is about this item. Used by a task: a task takes it, as its own item or beside it. Tasks in construction are not counted, and neither is what the package computes without serving it.

## The two axes

| | Subject | A piece of physics is filed here when |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Signal and contrast: what signal a tissue gives | it can be asked about one voxel |
| **B** | Spatial encoding and reconstruction: where the signal lands in the image | it can be asked on an object of uniform contrast |
| **C** | The system: what the machine adds: field, RF, gradients, noise, limits | it would be trivial on an ideal scanner |
| **D** | Image quality and artefacts: how good the image is, and what went wrong | it is about the whole image: SNR, contrast, resolution, time, artefacts |

| | Kind of task | What is delivered | For example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Measure | a quantity with its unit | T1 of a vial; the error of the centre frequency |
| **2** | Set | the setting that meets one requirement | the inversion time that nulls a tissue; the field of view without wrap |
| **3** | Trade | one protocol that meets several requirements at once | contrast, SNR and pixel size inside a time limit |
| **4** | Request | a scan for a stated purpose: the method is not named and the system has hidden properties | the fastest T1 map of a stated precision on an unfamiliar scanner |
| **5** | Design | the sequence itself: an RF pulse, a gradient waveform, the order and timing of its parts | a shorter slice-selective pulse inside the limits on peak B1 and RF power |

Kinds 1 to 3 are the knowledge, one piece at a time and then several together. Kind 4 asks for the best scan the console can give. Kind 5 lets the agent build what the console does not offer. A task of kind 3 or more names the simple items it brings together; whether training on the simple ones carries upward is a measurement, not a claim of this page.

## Formed in part

| | Item | What is missing | Waits for |
|---|---|---|---|
| A18 | Fat suppression by a frequency-selective saturation pulse | The pulse has a band, a centre and an efficiency, but it treats all fat as one line and its effect does not depend on repetition time or flip angle | ordinary engine work |
| A25 | Susceptibility-weighted imaging: the phase of a gradient echo as contrast | Phase images show the field of air cavities; no tissue has a susceptibility of its own (no veins, no iron) | 3D world |
| B17 | Partial Fourier: acquiring part of k-space | The lines left out are filled with zeros: the time saved and the blur are formed, the loss of SNR on a console is not | ordinary engine work |
| B20 | Three-dimensional encoding: a second phase-encode axis, the slab | A non-selective 3D scan is priced and its central partition is imaged; no slab profile, no fold along the slab | 3D world |
| C1 | Field strength: what changes between 1.5 T and 3 T | Two field strengths, one per session; nothing below 1.5 T or above 3 T | ordinary engine work |
| C3 | Centre frequency and its adjustment | The error of the adjustment can be measured; the console has no frequency setting (only the fat-saturation pulse can be retuned) | ordinary engine work |
| C5 | Magnetic susceptibility: the field around air and tissue boundaries | The field of a few air spheres is added in closed form; it is not computed from the susceptibility of the object | 3D world |
| C8 | Adiabatic pulses: an inversion that tolerates the transmit field | The console's inversion is one efficiency number; the hyperbolic-secant pulse and its threshold are computed in the design layer and played by no sequence | block-list core |
| C20 | Spoiler and crusher gradients: the moment and what survives it | The spoiler moment of a gradient echo is a parameter and acts on the signal; the crushers of a spin echo are ideal: what they dephase is gone, so there is no stimulated echo | block-list core |
| C22 | RF power: what raises B1+rms, and its limit | The console prices RF as B1+rms against a limit, from the nominal flip angle; there is no figure in W/kg | field model |
| D16 | Ghosts of periodic motion along the phase-encode axis | One tissue class pulses or shifts periodically; no irregular motion, and nothing moves through the slice | 3D world |

## Not formed yet

38 items. 26 of them wait for one of 7 pieces of engine work; the other 12 take only ordinary work on the present engine. "Computed" in the third column: the package already computes the item and checks it against a closed form or a second method, most of them in the design layer ([design](physics/design.md)), and no console sequence, parameter or task reaches it yet.

| Waits for | What it is | Items |
|---|---|---:|
| **3D world** | a volume with real structure through the slice, and volume and multi-slice encoding | 7 |
| **receive array** | several receive channels with sensitivity maps and noise correlation | 2 |
| **spin systems** | a density-matrix simulator for coupled spins | 1 |
| **field model** | Maxwell's equations on the slice for a body and a coil | 3 |
| **block-list core** | the Bloch and phase-graph signal core over a list of blocks, as the engine behind the console | 11 |
| **realistic anatomy** | textured digital anatomy instead of classes of one value each | 1 |
| **measured data** | measurements of public phantoms on real scanners, to compare with | 1 |
| ordinary engine work | nothing new: a term, a parameter or an option of the present engine | 12 |

### 3D world

A volume with real structure through the slice, and volume and multi-slice encoding.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| A24 | Perfusion: passage of a bolus, arterial spin labelling | - | No blood arrives through the plane and no tissue changes during the session |
| A26 | Quantitative susceptibility mapping | - | The field is known in one slice; going from the field to the susceptibility takes it in a volume |
| B4 | Several slices: slices per repetition, gap, order | - | A scan is one slice; the pulses of neighbouring slices are not played |
| B5 | Slice position, oblique planes, planning in three planes | - | The object is one axial section: there is no anatomy through the slice to place or tilt a slice in |
| C30 | Phantom tests: slice thickness and slice position | - | No test object has structure through the slice |
| D19 | Cross-talk between neighbouring slices | - | A scan is one slice |
| D20 | Metal: distortion of the slice itself, and the sequences against it | - | The slice is flat: how it bends near metal takes the third dimension |

| C23 | SAR in the body: whole-body and local heating | - | There is no body and no electric field of the coil: the console prices RF as B1+rms only |
| C26 | Implants and devices: scanning inside the conditions of a label | - | No object holds a device and no task states a label |
| C27 | The static field around the magnet: fringe field, forces on objects, zones, screening | - | The field outside the bore and the force on an object in it are not modelled |

### Block-list core

The Bloch and phase-graph signal core over a list of blocks, as the engine behind the console.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| A13 | Approach to the steady state: dummy cycles and the first lines of a scan | computed | The transient is computed by a separate chain of rotations; the scanner serves every line at the steady state |
| A14 | Echo trains: fast (turbo) spin echo, echo train length, effective echo time | computed | The design layer computes the echoes of a train of refocusing pulses, stimulated echoes included; no console sequence has an echo train, so no image is formed from one |
| A15 | Magnetisation preparation: saturation recovery, T2 preparation, prepared gradient echo | computed | An inversion-prepared gradient echo exists as a checked formula; the console prepares with inversion before a spin echo and with fat saturation only |
| A19 | Spatial saturation bands | - | There is no spatial saturation pulse |
| A20 | Magnetisation transfer and chemical exchange | - | Each tissue is one pool of protons |
| A21 | Diffusion weighting: b-value, apparent diffusion coefficient, tensor | computed | The design layer computes the b-value and b-tensor of a gradient program and the attenuated echo; no console sequence is diffusion-weighted (tissues have a diffusion coefficient that acts on the spoiling of gradient echoes only) |
| A22 | Flow: inflow, time-of-flight angiography, velocity encoding | - | Nothing flows: blood is a static tissue |
| B19 | Segmented acquisition and the order of the lines | - | Lines are acquired in one order, one per repetition (echo-planar: one shot) |
| C9 | RF pulse design: shaping a pulse to a profile | computed | The design layer generates pulses (windowed sinc, Shinnar-Le Roux, variable rate), simulates them and scores the profile against bounds on energy and duration; the console plays three fixed shapes and no task asks for a pulse |
| C21 | Gradient programs: lobes, moments and their nulling, the shortest waveform inside the limits | computed | The design layer computes moments, k-space and limit checks of a gradient program and the shortest lobe for given moments; the console builds its own trapezoids and no waveform can be entered |
| C24 | Nerve stimulation: the limit on dB/dt | computed | The design layer computes a stimulation figure of a gradient program from a declared model; the console plays gradients at one fixed slew rate and has no such limit |

### Realistic anatomy

Textured digital anatomy instead of classes of one value each.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| B26 | Reconstruction from incomplete data: compressed sensing and learned methods | - | The reconstruction is fixed, and objects made of classes of one value have no texture to judge such a method on |

### Measured data

Measurements of public phantoms on real scanners, to compare with.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| C33 | Agreement with measurement: a phantom on a real scanner against the same phantom here | - | No image of this engine has been compared with a measurement on a scanner |

### Ordinary engine work

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| A23 | Contrast agents: relaxivity and concentration | - | No material carries an agent; a dilution series could be built from vials |
| A27 | BOLD contrast and functional MRI | - | No tissue changes its T2* during the session, and a scan is not repeated as a series |
| B21 | Radial and spiral trajectories | - | Sampling is Cartesian |
| B24 | Options of the reconstruction: zero filling, filters, intensity and distortion correction | - | The image is the unfiltered transform of the acquired matrix |
| B25 | Raw data: looking at k-space, spikes | - | Only images leave the scanner |
| C4 | Shimming | - | The shim is fixed: the field can be mapped, not corrected |
| C13 | Receiver gain and dynamic range | - | Samples are floating-point numbers: no converter, no clipping |
| C17 | Gradient non-linearity: distortion away from the isocentre | - | A position warp exists for sensitivity checks only: it is checked against no reference and no task has it |
| C19 | Eddy currents and concomitant fields | - | Gradients are played as ideal trapezoids |
| C25 | Acoustic noise of the gradients | - | There is no model of sound |
| C32 | Stability over time: field drift, repeated scans | - | The system does not change during a session; a repeated scan differs by its noise only |
| D18 | Gating, triggering and breath-holding against motion | - | The console has no trigger: a scan is not synchronised with the motion |

## Where the list comes from

The items were drawn up from the tables of contents of 7 textbooks and from 10 teaching and examination outlines, read at the level of their headings. They are a map of topics; no examination item is reproduced.

- Bernstein, King, Zhou, Handbook of MRI Pulse Sequences
- Brown, Cheng, Haacke, Thompson, Venkatesan, Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Physical Principles and Sequence Design, 2nd ed.
- Nishimura, Principles of Magnetic Resonance Imaging
- McRobbie, Moore, Graves, Prince, MRI from Picture to Proton, 3rd ed.
- Liang, Lauterbur, Principles of Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Signal Processing Perspective
- Dale, Brown, Semelka, MRI: Basic Principles and Applications, 5th ed.
- Westbrook, Talbot, MRI in Practice, 5th ed.
- ARRT, MRI examination content specifications (2025)
- ABR, qualifying (core) exam physics study guide, section 13 (2023)
- AAPM, diagnostic radiology residents physics curriculum, module 13 (2018)
- AAPM Report 197, graduate programmes, section 3.2.5
- EFOMP, core curriculum for medical physicists in radiology, section 13 (2011)
- ASRT / AEIRS / SMRT, magnetic resonance curriculum (2015)
- IAEA, Diagnostic Radiology Physics handbook, chapters 14 and 15, with TCS-47
- ISMRM, weekend courses MR Physics and Engineering, Artifacts, Image Reconstruction (2022)
- ESMRMB, Practical MR Physics (2025)
- AAPM Report 100 with the ACR quality-control tests
